newsitem.title: INDONESIA: S.Korea says to boost LNG imports from Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea says to boost LNG imports from Indonesia.

text.p: South Korea has pledged to import more liquefied natural gas (LNG) from Indonesia and to boost cooperation in the energy sector, South Korea's Trade, Industry and Energy Minister Lim Chang-yeul said on Tuesday,
"I think the potential for even further cooperation between our two countries in energy and in the industrial sector is very high," he told reporters after meeting President Suharto.
"Demand for energy in Korea will increase very sharply. LNG is one area in which we will increase our imports," he said.
"We can make joint investments or increase imports from Indonesia," Lim added.

He gave no estimation of LNG imports, but the South Korean energy ministry has predicted LNG demand will rise to 18.2 million tonnes by 2000 from 12.1 million tonnes this year and 9.56 million last year.
The state-run Korea Gas Corp (KOGAS) said LNG imports were expected to rise to 20.7 milion tonnes in 2001 from 9.5 million tonnes in 1996.
KOGAS has said 5.3 million tonnes of LNG will imported from Indonesia by 2000.
Lim said Indonesia had an advantage in LNG transportation costs because it was close to Korea.
Indonesia's state oil company Pertamina on Monday broke ground for its eighth liquefied natural gas plant in East Kalimantan's Bontang town, saying it sought to expand its LNG export market.
Pertamina is currently committed to exporting more than 20 million tonnes of LNG to Japan, South Korea and Taiwan.
